title: Comparative Analysis of LiDAR and Photogrammetry for 3D Crime Scene Reconstruction
content: Accurate and fast 3D mapping of crime scenes is crucial in law enforcement, and first responders often need to document the scenes in detail under challenging conditions and within a limited time. Traditional methods often fail to capture the details to understand the scenes comprehensively. This study investigates the effectiveness of recent mobile phone-based mapping technologies equipped with a LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) sensor. The performance of LiDAR and pure photogrammetry is evaluated under different illumination (day and night) and scanning conditions (slow and fast scanning) in a mock-up crime scene. The results reveal that the mapping using an iPhone LIDAR in day-light conditions with 5 minutes of fast scanning shows the best results, yielding 0.1084 meters of error. Also, the cloud-to-cloud distance showed that 90% of the point clouds exhibited under 0.1224 meters of error, demonstrating the utility of these tools for rapid and portable scanning in crime scenes.
